whatItIs.text: The boiled sap of sugar, black, and red maples — concentrated until at least 66% sugar in Canada's rules; nothing else may be in the bottle.

historyNote.text: Maple syrup was first made by the Indigenous peoples of northeastern North America long before Europeans arrived; the Algonquians cut V-shaped incisions in the trunks and froze out the water overnight, and celebrated the first full moon of spring as the Sugar Moon.

howToChoose.text: Grade by colour: golden for delicate finishing, dark for strong baking; always read for 'pure maple syrup' — pancake syrup is usually flavoured corn syrup.

storage.text: Sealed it keeps in the cupboard; once open, refrigerate it.

useItUp.text: Maple sweetens dressings, glazes roast carrots or salmon, and freezes into cubes for coffee; any crystals re-dissolve with gentle warming.
